subject: SCIENCE
title: Animals Around Us
objective: Relate familiar animals to suitable habitats without disturbing wildlife.
introduction: A fish swims in a pond, a bird finds food near a nest, and a frog rests in a damp place. Why do these habitats fit?

vocabulary.definition: A place where living things find the resources they need.
A safe place that protects a living thing from danger.
A living thing that grows, moves, and needs food.

items.prompt: Milo sees a fish in a pond, a bird near a nest, and a frog on damp ground. Which statement is true?

options.text: Habitats provide resources such as food, water, shelter, and space.
Every animal fits one habitat only
A habitat is only a sleeping place

items.explanation: A habitat gives an animal resources such as food, water, shelter, and space. Different animals need different places, and a habitat is more than a sleeping spot.

items.prompt: Maxine helps an adult observe a tadpole. Which habitat is suitable for it?
items.explanation: Tadpoles and fish need water, so a water habitat can meet their needs. A tree, desert, or dry sand cannot provide the needed water.

items.prompt: Milo has four habitat cards. Which statement is NOT true?

options.text: Every animal fits one habitat only
Birds can find nesting places in trees

items.explanation: One habitat does not suit every animal because animals have different needs. Water can suit fish, trees can offer birds nesting space, and damp places suit frogs.

items.prompt: Maxine sees a tadpole swimming in a pond. Why might the pond suit it?

options.text: It provides water and resources it needs.
It gives the tadpole a school grade.

items.explanation: A pond provides water and other resources a tadpole needs while it grows. It is not made of paper, and not every animal can live there.

items.prompt: An earthworm is found under damp soil. Which environment suits it best?
items.explanation: Earthworms need moist soil for air, food, and shelter. An icebox, dry ocean surface, or hot sand does not provide the right conditions.
